item.research_question: How can PtRu-based high-entropy alloys be synthesized with subnanometer dimensions and tailored morphologies to achieve high activity, stability, and CO resistance for alkaline hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR)?
item.material_system: PtRuNiCoFeMo high-entropy alloy subnanometer nanowires (SNWs) with composition Pt/Ru/Ni/Co/Fe/Mo = 29.6/9.3/15.2/15.6/12.2/18.1 (SEM-EDS) or 28.5/6.8/18.6/15.2/10.7/20.2 (ICP-OES)
item.processing_route: Synthesis via solvothermal reduction: metal precursors (Pt(acac)2, Ru(acac)3, Ni(acac)2, Co(acac)3, Fe(acac)3, Mo(CO)6), glucose (reducing agent), and STAB (structure-directing agent) dissolved in oleylamine (OAm), heated at 210 °C for 5 h, followed by centrifugation and washing with cyclohexane/ethanol (1:9 v/v)
item.test_conditions: Alkaline HOR in 0.1 M KOH solution purged with H2; accelerated durability test (ADT) for 2000 cycles between -0.1 V and 0.4 V vs. RHE at 500 mV s-1; CO poisoning tests in 0.1 M KOH with 1000 ppm CO/H2; chronoamperometry at 100 mV vs. RHE
key_findings: Mass activity of HEA SNWs/C reached 6.75 A mgPt+Ru−1, which is 4.1 times higher than commercial PtRu/C (1.65 A mgPt+Ru−1) and 19.8 times higher than Pt/C (0.34 A mgPt+Ru−1)
Specific activity of HEA SNWs/C was 8.96 mA cm−2, 2.4 times higher than PtRu/C (3.77 mA cm−2) and 18.7 times higher than Pt/C (0.48 mA cm−2)
Only 6.2% loss in mass activity was observed after 2000 ADT cycles for HEA SNWs/C, compared to 20.6%, 31.5%, and 35.3% losses for HEA NPs/C, PtRu/C, and Pt/C respectively
In the presence of 1000 ppm CO, the limiting current density of HEA SNWs/C decreased by only 5.4% at 100 mV vs. RHE, whereas PtRu/C and Pt/C decreased by 21.3% and 22.7%
Chronoamperometry showed HEA SNWs/C activity decreased by 26.4% after 2000 s in 1000 ppm CO, while PtRu/C decreased by 82.9% and Pt/C completely deactivated after 1130 s
The d-band center of HEA SNWs/C shifted upwards to -3.835 eV compared to -3.732 eV for HEA NPs/C, weakening H* adsorption and facilitating OH* adsorption
DFT calculations revealed the energy barrier for H2O formation on HEA surface was as low as 0.08 eV, much lower than 0.57 eV for Pt and 0.27 eV for PtRu
The binding strength of H* on HEA SNWs/C was weakened to an appropriate level near 0 eV, while OH* binding on Ru was moderate at nearly -0.6 eV
item.mechanism: Strong electronic interactions between different metal sites in HEA SNWs regulate the binding strength of protons and hydroxyls; Co and Ni sites maintain stable valence states due to pinning effects by Fe and Mo, while Pt and Ru sites modulate overall electroactivity; the upshifted d-band center weakens H* adsorption and facilitates OH* adsorption, and the low energy barrier for H2O formation (0.08 eV) enables rapid desorption and superior HOR activity
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study, though it notes that controlled synthesis of PtRu-based HEAs with tailored morphologies remains a general challenge in the field
item.future_work: The authors propose that the work provides a viable synthetic route for fabricating Pt-based HEA subnano/nano materials and promotes fundamental research on catalysis and beyond
quotes: The mass and specific activities of HEA SNWs/C reach 6.75 A mgPt+Ru−1 and 8.96 mA cm−2, respectively
Density functional theory calculations reveal that the strong interactions between different metal sites in HEA SNWs can greatly regulate the binding strength of proton and hydroxyl
The energy barrier for H2O formation on HEA surface is as low as 0.08 eV, which is much lower than that of Pt and PtRu

records.text: Paper card. Question: How can PtRu-based high-entropy alloys be synthesized with subnanometer dimensions and tailored morphologies to achieve high activity, stability, and CO resistance for alkaline hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR)?. System: PtRuNiCoFeMo high-entropy alloy subnanometer nanowires (SNWs) with composition Pt/Ru/Ni/Co/Fe/Mo = 29.6/9.3/15.2/15.6/12.2/18.1 (SEM-EDS) or 28.5/6.8/18.6/15.2/10.7/20.2 (ICP-OES). Processing: Synthesis via solvothermal reduction: metal precursors (Pt(acac)2, Ru(acac)3, Ni(acac)2, Co(acac)3, Fe(acac)3, Mo(CO)6), glucose (reducing agent), and STAB (structure-directing agent) dissolved in oleylamine (OAm), heated at 210 °C for 5 h, followed by centrifugation and washing with cyclohexane/ethanol (1:9 v/v). Test conditions: Alkaline HOR in 0.1 M KOH solution purged with H2; accelerated durability test (ADT) for 2000 cycles between -0.1 V and 0.4 V vs. RHE at 500 mV s-1; CO poisoning tests in 0.1 M KOH with 1000 ppm CO/H2; chronoamperometry at 100 mV vs. RHE. Findings: Mass activity of HEA SNWs/C reached 6.75 A mgPt+Ru−1, which is 4.1 times higher than commercial PtRu/C (1.65 A mgPt+Ru−1) and 19.8 times higher than Pt/C (0.34 A mgPt+Ru−1); Specific activity of HEA SNWs/C was 8.96 mA cm−2, 2.4 times higher than PtRu/C (3.77 mA cm−2) and 18.7 times higher than Pt/C (0.48 mA cm−2); Only 6.2% loss in mass activity was observed after 2000 ADT cycles for HEA SNWs/C, compared to 20.6%, 31.5%, and 35.3% losses for HEA NPs/C, PtRu/C, and Pt/C respectively; In the presence of 1000 ppm CO, the limiting current density of HEA SNWs/C decreased by only 5.4% at 100 mV vs. RHE, whereas PtRu/C and Pt/C decreased by 21.3% and 22.7%; Chronoamperometry showed HEA SNWs/C activity decreased by 26.4% after 2000 s in 1000 ppm CO, while PtRu/C decreased by 82.9% and Pt/C completely deactivated after 1130 s; The d-band center of HEA SNWs/C shifted upwards to -3.835 eV compared to -3.732 eV for HEA NPs/C, weakening H* adsorption and facilitating OH* adsorption; DFT calculations revealed the energy barrier for H2O formation on HEA surface was as low as 0.08 eV, much lower than 0.57 eV for Pt and 0.27 eV for PtRu; The binding strength of H* on HEA SNWs/C was weakened to an appropriate level near 0 eV, while OH* binding on Ru was moderate at nearly -0.6 eV. Mechanism: Strong electronic interactions between different metal sites in HEA SNWs regulate the binding strength of protons and hydroxyls; Co and Ni sites maintain stable valence states due to pinning effects by Fe and Mo, while Pt and Ru sites modulate overall electroactivity; the upshifted d-band center weakens H* adsorption and facilitates OH* adsorption, and the low energy barrier for H2O formation (0.08 eV) enables rapid desorption and superior HOR activity. Limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study, though it notes that controlled synthesis of PtRu-based HEAs with tailored morphologies remains a general challenge in the field. Future work: The authors propose that the work provides a viable synthetic route for fabricating Pt-based HEA subnano/nano materials and promotes fundamental research on catalysis and beyond. Quote: "The mass and specific activities of HEA SNWs/C reach 6.75 A mgPt+Ru−1 and 8.96 mA cm−2, respectively"
